summary.name: Performance Monitor
summary.one_liner: A lightweight, open-source menu bar system monitor for macOS showing CPU, memory, network, disk, GPU, temperatures and battery.
use_cases: Watching CPU, memory and temperatures from the menu bar
Getting alerts when CPU, memory, disk or temperature exceed thresholds
Checking SSD wear and battery health
Finding which processes use the most CPU
Logging system metrics to CSV for analysis
Monitoring a Mac without sending data to third parties
summary.what_it_does: Performance Monitor is a menu bar app for macOS that displays CPU, memory, network, disk, GPU, temperature and battery metrics. You can choose which metrics appear in the menu bar as text or live sparklines, with optional threshold colouring. Deep detail windows show per-core CPU, process breakdowns, latency and throughput charts, per-sensor temperatures, fan speeds, SSD wear level and battery health. It sends native notifications when CPU, memory, disk or temperature cross set thresholds, and can optionally save CSV history. The page says it has no telemetry, analytics or accounts, and that sampling pauses when nothing is on screen.
notable: Open source with public source code on GitHub
No telemetry, analytics or accounts; updates are Ed25519-signed and verified before install
Pauses sampling when nothing is on screen to stay lightweight
caveats: Requires an Apple Silicon Mac (M1 or later) on macOS 14+
Not notarised by Apple, so first launch needs right-click → Open
Developer relies on donations (GitHub Sponsors, Ko-fi) toward the Apple Developer Program fee needed for notarisation
